root_idea.summary: The root centers on gathering and rising: the head is the gathered or elevated upper part, and this develops into meanings of prominence, leadership, priority, and beginnings.
root_idea.development: From the bodily head and the uppermost point, Classical Arabic extends the root to chiefs, principal or essential parts, beginnings, things that rise ahead, and related figurative constructions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The canonical Quranic noun is a distinct public dictionary form under the citation headword رَأْس.

senses.definition: The head of a human or animal; the bodily upper part.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic occurrences use the singular and plural with possessive pronouns and in constructions involving shaving, raising, bowing, grasping, or having something poured over the head. The plural also occurs in the image of the heads of devils.

senses.definition: The principal sum or capital of property.
senses.usage_conditions: A specialized construction meaning the principal of a loan or property; the Quranic occurrence at 2:279 is the plural in this capital/principal sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hit or hurt someone on the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may take the head as the object of striking, including striking it with a staff.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be affected or overcome by a head ailment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of having a complaint or illness of the head, including the disease called بِرْسَام.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become head, chief, commander, ruler, or superior over people; to be high in rank or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may occur with a people or with عَلَى indicating authority over them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive for or desire headship or command.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative use with رِئَاسَةٌ as the desired position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a lizard, to turn or come forth with its head foremost toward an adversary or from its hole.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The head-first orientation is contrasted with coming forth tail-first.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make or appoint someone head, chief, commander, or ruler over a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative appointment construction takes the person appointed as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or be made head, chief, commander, or ruler over people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى or عَلَيْهِمْ for assuming or receiving authority over a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become mounted or fixed upon the head of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical image is of an object settling onto or becoming fixed on a head, including the point of a spear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take someone by the neck and lower the head toward the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive physical construction illustrated with a named person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To occupy or divert someone so as to draw away their attention.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension associated with the preceding act of taking or lowering someone by the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The highest, uppermost, or top part of a thing, including the upper part of a mountain or valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the spatial extension from the bodily head; a valley's upper part may be called its head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kiss someone's head, expressed metonymically as reaching or striking the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional metonymical phrase rather than a literal act of striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away from someone, pay no attention to them, or hold a bad opinion of them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic expression literally framed as being shot by someone into the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One after another or in close succession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing births or other events occurring head after head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Uniform, of one way, mode, or manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in a construction meaning to make a thing one-headed, hence consistent or of a single pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An individual animal counted as one head of livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a counting unit for sheep, goats, and other beasts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bulb or head of garlic.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cloves are treated as subdivisions of the garlic head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity, end, or last part of a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a spatial extension of the head as the terminal or foremost part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A headland, cape, or promontory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical projection or extremity is named by the head term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hilt or pommel of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources distinguish the hilt from, or identify it with, the pommel, with some lexical uncertainty about the exact form رِيَاس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either of the two nodes of a planet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical astronomical expression, الرَّأْسُ وَالذَّنَبُ, literally “the head and the tail.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief, leader, or person of authority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use synonymous with رَئِيسٌ, including a leader of a people or a group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The principal, essential, or foundational part of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively for what is most essential, including the foundational part of a discipline or matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The beginning or first part of a period, affair, or undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for the beginning of a month, year, affair, or speech, and for the initial stage of an undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To begin again from the start or repeat something from its beginning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiom “from the head” when asking someone to repeat speech from the beginning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be on the point of accomplishing an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for being at the threshold or initial stage of completing one's business.

other_classical_meanings.definition: During a person's lifetime or in their time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression “on the head of so-and-so” can mark the time in which that person was alive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A numerous and strong company of people, an army in its own right.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective singular use describing a group strong enough not to need assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel retaining fat only in its head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of an emaciated camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One struck or injured in the head, including one whose head has been broken and its skin cleft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a lexical use of the headword رَئِيسٌ distinct from its leadership sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person affected or overcome by a head disease or complaint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes affliction by بِرْسَام or another ailment of the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A chief, leader, ruler, or person high in rank or condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also designate the chief among animals, such as the leading dog in a chase.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Principal or vital parts of an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the technical expression الأعضاء الرئيسة, the listed vital organs are the heart, brain, liver, and testicles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seller of animal heads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational noun; the alternative forms with و are identified as vulgar, incorrect, or post-classical by the source.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who is often made, appointed, or becomes a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive form expresses repeated or habitual acquisition of headship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hunting bitch that seizes or springs upon the head of the quarry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form may be used alongside the masculine form in this specialized hunting description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything elevated or rising above the adjacent parts; especially the upper part of a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural رَوَائِسُ is used for the uppermost parts of valleys.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cloud that precedes the other clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of being foremost; the source notes uncertainty about the grammatical form in one citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large-headed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man, sheep or goat, or stallion, with related forms differing in their attested animal applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or she-goat with a black head and face while the rest of the body is white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-color description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A head strong or inclined to butt or knock against other heads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related plural describes heads that engage in such butting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lizard coming forth from its hole head foremost.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is opposed to مُذَنِّبٌ, one coming forth tail foremost.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical designation recorded independently of the lizard description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that bites the heads of competing horses or takes precedence in a race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve both the head-biting description and the broader sense of being foremost in racing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One whose desire or sexual appetite is only in his head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of desire localized in the head, not the general passive sense of being under a chief.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A subject or subordinate of a chief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive relation to a رَئِيس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who holds back from the party to which he belongs in fighting or battle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized military or group-behavior description.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Illustrates the ordinary plural head sense.
Identifies an active participle without adding lexical content.

cautions: The Quranic noun is overwhelmingly literal “head,” but 2:279 uses the established construction for principal capital.
Several Classical entries are specialized, figurative, or dialectally qualified; their usage conditions preserve those restrictions without treating them as Quranic senses.
